newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand was charting fresh five-month lows late Tuesday after yielding to a day-long push at the 4.55 level fuelled by offshore dollar demand and nervousness about the gold price.
The rand was last quoted at 4.5500/5530 on the U.S. dollar from 4.5355/5385 late Monday, having earlier hit an intraday worst of 4.5505, a level not seen since February 3.
Dealers said the move through 4.55, prompted by a late bout of offshore dollar demand, had been kept orderly by the Reserve Bank "smoothing" activities.

"I think the central bank's trying to engineer a smooth move up to 4.5600. It seems to to be happy to let it gap up and let it trade sideways for a while," said one Johannesburg-based foreign exchange dealer.
The market concensus was that 4.56 would be the unit's short-term ceiling but just how far the Reserve Bank would let it go in the longer term was unclear.
"I don't think the bank's actually unhappy given the state of the gold price. They're using a slow, co-ordinated strategy but where it all ends I'm not that sure," said one dealer.
The rand took little heart from a slight rebound by gold in London dealings, with the yellow metal's upside probably limited after prices slumped to 12-year lows last week.
In cross rate dealings the rand started stronger against the Japanese yen and German mark but weaker against the British pound.

But the unit's strength against the mark faded with it last fetching 0.3860/3864 marks from 0.3842/3845 on Monday. Gains against the yen were also whittled with the rand last at 24.6944/7326 yen from 24.7318/7702.
Against sterling the rand found its lowest point since January 22 during the session recovering only slightly to stand at 7.6931/7028 pounds from 7.6404/6500 before.
South African gilts had a comparatively frothy session with yields tracking steadily lower on options and eurobond hedging-related demand.
The benchmark R150 bond was last changing hands at 14.110 percent from Monday's 1405 GMT level of 14.195 pct.
"The jobbers were trying to sell it down earlier but then the Americans came in and swept them up. It was pretty messy today, not much volume," said one bond dealer.
Other dealers said the debt market was likely to get nervous a these levels with the softer rand and weaker U.S. rates looming as negative indicators.
On the money market, three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.65 to 15.70 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged between 15.25 and 15.10 percent.
The R150 was likely to run into selling between 14.05 and 14.00 percent while upside resistance for Wednesday's session was pegged around 14.20.
On the money market, three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.65 to 15.70 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged between 15.25 and 15.10 percent.
South Africa's money market shortage rose to 6.284 billion rand on Monday from 5.781 billion rand on Saturday, the Reserve Bank said.
Foreigners were net buyers of 344.25 million rand's worth of bonds on Monday after buying 1,016.37 million rand's worth on Friday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal cumulative volumes stood at 5.1 billion rand on Monday.
-- Justin McCamish, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482-1003
